headline: Load-generator's synthetic traffic to the storefront has been completely dark for 65+ min (since 09:57 UTC, flag off since 07:22:52 UTC) -- the app itself is verified healthy by direct probe, but with zero real traffic this environment currently has no ability to detect any regression, including whether inc-001 has actually recovered.
blast_radius: No confirmed real-user impact: manual GET to the storefront homepage and to a live product page both returned HTTP 200 in <120ms, and the product-page call visibly incremented product-catalog's own GetProduct OK counter -- the full frontend-proxy -> frontend -> product-catalog path is live and correctly wired right now. The actual harm is an observability blind spot: the load-generator is the only traffic source that exercises this sandbox, and it has driven zero real application requests for over an hour, which also directly blocks confirming recovery of inc-001.
reasoning: DECLARE, not ATTACH to inc-001: the mechanism is a different flag (loadGeneratorTraffic, 'Turn off to pause all load-generator scenarios') with a different effect (stops traffic generation entirely, vs. productCatalogFailure which injects errors into served requests), confirmed via the load-generator's own log line ('loadGeneratorTraffic evaluated to 0' first at 07:22:52 UTC) and independently reconfirmed by this run's own flag check at 10:53:36Z (loadGeneratorTraffic defaultVariant=off). The ~07:19-07:22 UTC timing sits close to inc-001's error-spike onset (~07:27-07:56 UTC), but overlap in time is not proof of relatedness per this skill's own heuristic -- there is no log or trace tying the load-generator's container restart to product-catalog's flag evaluation, so treating these as two incidents rather than forcing a merge on a coincidental clock.

rca.root_cause: This is a configuration/environment-level fault, not a code bug. The sandbox's live flagd instance currently evaluates `loadGeneratorTraffic` to its 'off' variant -- a deviation from the flag's shipped upstream default of 'on' in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo's src/flagd/demo.flagd.json (defaultVariant: 'on', variants {off:0, on:1}). That upstream file is where load-generator's app code and this environment's config part ways: nothing in load-generator's own code turned this off. src/load-generator/script.js's httpScenario() and browserScenario() both open by calling getFlagdValue('loadGeneratorTraffic') and, exactly by design, sleep and return without generating any traffic whenever the value is <=0 -- the silence since 09:57 UTC (and the flag reading 'off' continuously since 07:22:52 UTC per its own logged evaluations) is the load-generator correctly honoring an externally-set flag state, not a defect. Re-checking flagd's live /list just now (11:35 UTC) also shows two other flags currently deviating from their upstream shipped defaults in the same direction -- cartFailure (upstream default 'off', live 'on') and recommendationCacheFailure (upstream default 'off', live 'on') -- corroborating that this environment's flag store has been externally modified away from shipped defaults as a matter of course (the same class of mechanism as inc-001's productCatalogFailure override), not that load-generator's own state drifted on its own. Because nothing in load-generator polls or resets this flag over time, it will not self-revert -- it stays off until whatever set it changes it back. This project's own rules forbid any capability from calling flagd's /toggle, so this is neither this agent's to fix nor a code-level incident: absence of a code cause is the correct and complete answer here. Whether the specific 07:22:52 UTC flip was deliberately paired with inc-001's fault-injection or an unrelated stuck toggle remains genuinely undetermined -- no log or trace ties the two flag changes to a single triggering event, only their live-deviates-from-shipped-default pattern in common.
rca.verify_detail: A fresh, blind sub-agent independently re-fetched both files from the real open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo repo (not given this reasoning, only the two literal claims) and confirmed: (1) src/flagd/demo.flagd.json defines loadGeneratorTraffic with defaultVariant:'on', state ENABLED, variants {off:0, on:1} verbatim; (2) src/load-generator/script.js's getFlagdValue() POSTs to the OFREP evaluate endpoint, and both httpScenario() and browserScenario() guard on `getFlagdValue('loadGeneratorTraffic') <= 0` to skip traffic generation, matching the claimed by-design behavior. Both CONFIRMED against real fetched content, not a plausible-sounding guess.

remediation.second_opinion: Round 1 (FLAGGED): 'FLAGGED -- for an internal inconsistency in the proposal's own mechanism, not for overreach in principle. The proposal explicitly disclaims touching cartFailure or recommendationCacheFailure, calling that scope creep. But its first concrete implementation option -- reload or restart the flagd instance backing this environment from that unmodified upstream flag-configuration file -- would reload the entire flag set from the upstream file, resetting all three currently-deviating flags (including the two it says it is deliberately leaving alone) back to their shipped defaults. Only the second option it offers (a scoped OFREP/admin update to loadGeneratorTraffic alone) actually honors the stated scope... Separately worth flagging: three flags deviating from upstream defaults simultaneously in the same live sandbox is suspicious.' Round 2, after revision dropping the reload/restart path and adding the shared-fault-injection-state caveat (FINAL, CLEAN): 'The specific defect from the prior round is fixed: the proposal now names only a scoped OFREP/admin update to loadGeneratorTraffic, and explicitly rules out the reload/restart path that would have wholesale-reset cartFailure and recommendationCacheFailure. The stated scope and the concrete mechanism now match. The added caveat is substantive, not decorative... Overreach: none. Hiding the issue: no. Hardcoding: no. Self-toggle line: this is a genuine handoff, not the capability performing the write itself. No further issues found. Proposal is sound as revised.'
remediation.summary: Verified root cause is a live flagd runtime override (loadGeneratorTraffic stuck at 'off' vs. shipped upstream default 'on'), not a code defect -- proposing a scoped flagd config update to restore it to 'on' (leaving unrelated deviated flags cartFailure/recommendationCacheFailure untouched), with no diff and no PR since nothing in the versioned repo is wrong; full rationale in remediations/incident-002/rationale.md.

release_approval.own_re_review: Independently confirmed there is nothing to review or merge, not merely that remediation says so. (1) remediation.pr_url is null and remediation.type is config_proposal, not code_fix; (2) re-checked the onboarded repo's PR list myself via `gh pr list --repo <team repo> --state all` -- no open, merged, or closed PR references incident-002 or loadGeneratorTraffic; (3) re-read remediations/incident-002/rationale.md and the verified RCA directly: implicated_file and implicated_function are both null, and rca.verify_detail shows a blind sub-agent independently re-fetched the real upstream open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo files and confirmed loadGeneratorTraffic's shipped defaultVariant is already 'on' -- the versioned repo is already correct, so a diff against it would have nothing to fix. The actual proposed change is a live flagd OFREP/admin write, which is explicitly outside this or any capability's allowed tool surface (/toggle is off-limits project-wide) and outside release-approval's mandate, which is scoped to reviewing a diff before `gh pr merge`. My four standard checks (source re-fetch, diff minimality/scope, no reckless pattern, syntactic validity) do not apply to a non-existent diff, so none were skippable-but-skipped -- there is nothing to run them against. Nothing here required or permitted a merge action.

escalation.observed: loadGeneratorTraffic has evaluated to 0/off continuously since 07:22:52 UTC (3.5+ hours by the time of this run), the load-generator's VU count and its own flagd-polling traffic never stopped (process is alive and busy), and all app-facing traffic (frontend-proxy, frontend, product-catalog, cart, checkout) flatlined completely at 09:57 UTC and has stayed flat since.
escalation.ruled_out: Not an app outage (direct probes succeeded, 200 OK, real counter increment); not a load-generator process crash (k6_vus steady at 6, flagd-polling traffic climbing the entire time); not an observability-pipeline failure (otelcol-contrib and load-generator's own telemetry never stopped flowing -- only the app-request counters went flat).
escalation.open_question: Why has loadGeneratorTraffic remained off for 3.5+ hours after the load-generator's restart, and was that restart itself deliberate (part of the same fault-injection scenario as inc-001) or an unrelated stuck/failed restart? This determines whether traffic should be expected to resume on its own or needs an explicit fix -- handing to root-cause-analysis, since alert-grouping cannot determine intent behind a flag state from metrics/logs alone.
